versions.statement: Given sets $A = \{1, 2, 3\}$ and $B = \{2, 3, 4\}$, find $A \cup B$ and $A \cap B$.
versions.description: The union $A \cup B = \{1, 2, 3, 4\}$ contains all elements that are in either set.\nThe intersection $A \cap B = \{2, 3\}$ contains elements that are in both sets.
versions.hints: Recall: union collects elements in either set; intersection keeps only elements common to both.
versions.notes: Direct application of set union and intersection definitions.

versions.statement: Given functions $f(x) = x^2$ and $g(x) = x+1$, find $(f \circ g)(x)$ and $(g \circ f)(x)$.
versions.hints: Use the definition $(f \circ g)(x) = f(g(x))$ and substitute carefully.

versions.description: A set is a collection of distinct objects, considered as an object in its own right.|||In mathematics, a set is a well-defined collection of distinct objects.
Basic operations on sets include union, intersection, difference, and complement.|||Set operations provide ways to combine and compare sets.
versions.notes: Important for understanding relationships between sets

versions.description: A function $f: X \rightarrow Y$ is a relation that associates each element $x \in X$ with exactly one element $y \in Y$.|||Functions map elements from a domain to a codomain with each input having exactly one output.
versions.notes: Key concept in all areas of mathematics
